title: Block: Union-Find
oneLiner: Process friendship logs in time order with union-find and return the moment everyone becomes connected.
keyTakeaway: Union-find is two short functions: find follows parents to the root (pointing nodes at it as it goes), and union joins two roots. Keep a component count and decrease it only when the roots differ.
explanation:
n people, 0 to n - 1. logs holds [time, a, b], sorted by time: a and b become friends. Friendship is transitive. Return the earliest time at which everyone is connected, or -1 if that never happens.

parent[i] = i to start and count = n. find(x) walks up to the root and sets parent links along the way to the root (path compression). union(a, b) finds both roots; if they differ, attach the lower-rank root under the other and decrease count. Return the log's time when count reaches 1. Redundant Connection, Kruskal's MST and Accounts Merge are this block.

starterCode.python:
def earliest_all_connected(n, logs):
    # 1. Make parent[i] = i, a rank array, and a component count of n.
    # 2. Write find(x): follow parents to the root and point the nodes on the way at it (path compression).
    # 3. Write union(a, b): find both roots; if they differ, attach the lower-rank root under the other and decrease the count.
    # 4. Process the logs in order; when the count reaches 1, return that log's time.
    # 5. If it never does, return -1.
    return -1

gotchas: Setting parent[a] = b instead of joining the roots, which loses everything already attached to a.
Decreasing the count when the two are already in the same set.

complexity.note: With path compression and union by rank each operation is close to O(1) (inverse Ackermann), so the logs take about O(E); without both it is O(log V) per call. The parent and rank arrays are O(V).
